item.title: Sat 14 Nov 06:40 · risk-off · Bitcoin breaks below its four-year average as ETF exodus hits seven days
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Bitcoin slipped overnight to about $66,400 on Kraken, its lowest since mid-August, and traded near $67,310 at 06:32 UK, below its 200-week average of about $68,000.
  2. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $185.4 million on Friday, a seventh straight day of outflows, almost all from BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC, according to SoSoValue.
  3. Fed Governor Philip Jefferson said inflation remains well above target, with core PCE at 3.1%, and that the next move depends on the data, keeping talk of higher rates alive.

What changed: At last night's edition bitcoin was near $68,260 and resting on its 200-week average. It has since broken below that line in thin weekend trade, about 1.4% lower. Friday's ETF figures confirmed the outflow streak has reached seven days. Zcash eased to about $922, still steadier than bitcoin over the week. Next to watch: The weekly close on Sunday night, then Nvidia results on Tuesday 17 November after the US close. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Bitcoin breaks below its four-year average as ETF exodus hits seven days

Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since mid-August in early Saturday trading, slipping beneath its 200-week moving average after another day of withdrawals from US spot funds.

Bitcoin dropped to about $66,400 on Kraken overnight and traded near $67,310 at 06:32 UK on Saturday, roughly $950 below where it stood at the close of US trading on Friday evening.

The fall took it beneath its 200-week moving average, about $68,000, a long-run trend line it first touched on Friday for the first time in 11 weeks, Cointelegraph reported. Finwire, citing CryptoPotato, said it was bitcoin's lowest level since mid-August, and that nearly $700 million of leveraged positions had been liquidated over the past day, according to CoinGlass.

US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of $185.4 million on Friday, the seventh session in a row, according to SoSoValue data reported by TokenPost. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5 million and Fidelity's FBTC for $41.9 million. The funds lost more than $1.8 billion in the first eight trading days of November, BTC Pulse's tally of Farside and SoSoValue figures showed.

The selling came as Federal Reserve Governor Philip Jefferson said on Friday that inflation remained well above the Fed's 2% goal, with core PCE at 3.1% in September, and that future policy moves would depend on the data.

Weekend trading is typically thin. US markets reopen on Monday, and Nvidia reports results on Tuesday after the close.

Bitcoin slid overnight to about $66,400, its lowest since mid-August, and sits near $67,300 below its 200-week average. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $185 million on Friday, a seventh straight day of outflows.

Finwire, citing CryptoPotato, called it the lowest level since mid-August and put liquidations at nearly $700 million over the past day, per CoinGlass. Kraken (price data) Finwire (citing CryptoPotato) Cointelegraph
  2. 🟠 Developing ETFs and Institutions: Spot bitcoin ETFs lose $185 million on Friday, a seventh straight outflow (High confidence). This answers last night's open question: outflows continued. IBIT lost $143.5 million and FBTC $41.9 million, and the other ten funds were flat, according to SoSoValue data reported by TokenPost; Bloomingbit reported the same total from Farside. November outflows passed $1.8 billion in the first eight trading days, per BTC Pulse. TokenPost (citing SoSoValue) Bloomingbit (citing Farside) BTC Pulse
  3. 🟠 New The Big Picture: Fed's Jefferson: inflation still well above target, moves depend on the data (High confidence). In a speech in San Diego, Governor Philip Jefferson said core PCE inflation was 3.1% and headline 3.6% in September, partly from energy and demand for AI chips, with unemployment at 4.1%. He gave no hint of cuts, which keeps the higher-rates backdrop that has weighed on bitcoin this month. Federal Reserve
  4. 🟢 Developing Zcash Desk: Zcash eases to about $922 but holds up better than bitcoin (High confidence). ZEC traded near $922 on Kraken at 06:32 UK, down from $938 last night, after a 24-hour range of $891 to $992. Finwire listed it among the few large coins to hold small gains over the past day. No Zcash-specific news explained the move. Kraken (price data) Finwire (citing CryptoPotato)
  5. 🟢 New Zcash Desk: Zcash Q4 retroactive grants enter review, including an audited zcashd alternative (High confidence). The coinholder-directed retroactive grant programme opened its review period, with applications including an audited zcashd replacement from Zec.rocks, shielded voting and core protocol work, according to the Zcash forum. It sits alongside the coinholder polls opening on Monday. Zcash Community Forum
  6. 🟢 New Whale Watch: Bitcoin wallets dormant for 16 years move $6.9 million (Medium confidence). Decrypt reported that early-era wallets untouched since about 2010 moved roughly $6.9 million of bitcoin. A transfer is not proof of a sale, and the sum is small next to daily ETF flows. Decrypt

item.title: Fri 13 Nov 21:35 · risk-off · Stocks claw back losses but bitcoin stays pinned near $68,000
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Wall Street closed mixed after a volatile day: the S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.9%, while the Dow edged up 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St, so stocks recovered much of their midday slide.
  2. Bitcoin did not join the recovery. It traded near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 4.4% down on the day, sitting on its 200-week average near $68,000, and CoinDesk said it is on course for a sixth weekly loss.
  3. President Trump sent bipartisan nominees for the short-handed SEC and CFTC to the Senate, Bitcoin Magazine reported, with the Clarity Act market-structure bill still stalled.

What changed: This afternoon bitcoin was near $68,700 and the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%. Stocks have since cut their losses, but bitcoin has drifted slightly lower, so the gap between crypto and equities widened into the close. Friday's ETF flow figures are not yet out. Zcash has given back some of its afternoon gain, to about $938. Next to watch: Friday's ETF flow figures overnight, then Nvidia results on Tuesday 17 November after the US close. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Stocks claw back losses but bitcoin stays pinned near $68,000

Wall Street recovered much of a midday sell-off by Friday's close, but bitcoin ended the US session about 4% lower, resting on its 200-week average and heading for a sixth weekly fall.

Bitcoin traded near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK on Friday, about 4.4% below where it started the day, after US stock markets closed well off their lows.

The S&P 500 finished 0.4% lower and the Nasdaq 0.9% lower, while the Dow Jones rose 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St. At midday in New York the Nasdaq had been down about 1.6%, Yahoo Finance reported, as Nvidia's leadership turmoil and a 10-year Treasury yield of up to 5.17% weighed on technology shares.

Bitcoin did not share in the late recovery. It is sitting on its 200-week moving average, about $67,993, which it slipped below on Friday for the first time in 11 weeks, Cointelegraph reported. CoinDesk said bitcoin is on course for its sixth weekly loss in a row and is down 11% in November.

CoinDesk also pointed to next week's expected initial public offering of Anthropic, which is seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion on Nasdaq, as one possible reason investors were freeing up cash. That link is a suggestion, not an established cause.

US spot bitcoin ETFs had six straight days of outflows to Thursday. Friday's figures are due overnight. Nvidia reports results on Tuesday, and the Fed's December decision follows on 9 December.

US stocks recovered most of Friday's tech sell-off by the close, but bitcoin stayed about 4% lower near $68,260, on its 200-week average and heading for a sixth weekly loss. Bipartisan SEC and CFTC nominees went to the Senate.

  1. 🔴 Developing Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin ends the US session near $68,260, on its 200-week average (High confidence). Since this afternoon's $68,700, bitcoin has drifted lower even as stocks recovered, trading near $68,260 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 4.4% down on the day (range $67,500 to $71,540). Cointelegraph put the 200-week moving average at about $67,993, first touched in 11 weeks. CoinDesk said bitcoin is heading for a sixth straight weekly loss, down 11% in November and 21% in 2026. Kraken (price data) Cointelegraph CoinDesk
  2. 🟠 Outlook changed Markets: Wall Street closes mixed, well off its midday lows (Medium confidence). This afternoon the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%. By the 21:00 UK close it was down 0.9%, the S&P 500 0.4%, and the Dow was up 0.1%, according to 24/7 Wall St. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.17% during the day, Yahoo Finance reported. The late rebound eases the tech-shock picture for stocks, though not for bitcoin. 24/7 Wall St Yahoo Finance
  3. 🟠 New Markets: Anthropic's planned listing next week cited as a drain on risk cash (Medium confidence). CoinDesk reported that Anthropic aims to raise up to $64.4 billion in a Nasdaq listing next week, with Bloomberg saying orders are about six times the shares on offer. CoinDesk suggested investors may be raising cash for it, noting bitcoin fell from about $75,000 to $60,000 in the days before SpaceX's June listing. CoinDesk (citing Bloomberg)
  4. 🟠 New Policy: Trump sends bipartisan SEC and CFTC nominees to the Senate (Medium confidence). Nominees are Kristin Johnson (Democrat) and Steven Levine (Republican) for the SEC, and Nathan Anonick (Republican) and Matthew Rowland (Democrat) for the CFTC, Bitcoin Magazine reported. The SEC has two commissioners and the CFTC one. The Clarity Act failed a Senate vote 49 to 50 in September and lapses on 3 January unless revived, so the agencies are setting crypto policy on their own for now. Bitcoin Magazine CoinDesk
  5. 🟢 Developing Zcash Desk: Zcash slips back to about $938 (High confidence). ZEC was near $954 this afternoon after a high of $992. It traded near $938 on Kraken at 21:35 UK, about 1.9% down on the day, still holding up better than bitcoin. No Zcash-specific news explained the move. Kraken (price data)
  6. 🟢 New UK: RUSI calls crypto laundering a 'material risk' for the UK before its FATF review (Medium confidence). A RUSI taskforce said the UK's crypto regime starts on 25 October 2027, after FATF assessors visit in June 2027, and warned that high-risk assets such as USDT could sit outside FCA oversight, Decrypt reported. It is background for how strict FCA rules and HMRC reporting may become. Decrypt
  7. 🟢 New Policy: US moves to seize $1.2 billion of the Binance hack proceeds (Medium confidence). The Justice Department obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen from Binance on 29 October, which the FBI attributes to North Korea, Cointelegraph reported. More than $2.7 billion has been frozen in all. It reduces the overhang of stolen coins that could be sold. Cointelegraph
  8. 🟢 New Protocol and Development: Unstoppable Wallet team reports Zcash wallet sync about 21 times faster (Low confidence). A forum post says a new 'Slipstream' engine restored a Zcash wallet on an iPhone in under 10 minutes against a projected three and a half hours. Slow sync has long been a usability complaint for shielded Zcash wallets. Zcash Community Forum

Information only, not advice.

item.title: Fri 13 Nov 16:45 · risk-off · Bitcoin's PPI bounce fades as tech sell-off drags Wall Street
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. US producer prices rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast, and bitcoin jumped to $70,190 on Kraken within the hour of the 13:30 UK release.
  2. The bounce did not hold: after Wall Street opened, the Nasdaq fell about 1.6% on Nvidia's leadership turmoil, the 10-year yield touched 5.16%, and bitcoin slipped back to about $68,700 by 16:45 UK.
  3. Final figures put Thursday's US spot bitcoin ETF outflows at $284 million, a sixth straight day, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $204 million, according to SoSoValue data.

What changed: This morning bitcoin was near $68,900 after the overnight flush to $67,500. A softer PPI gave a brief lift above $70,000, but US stocks turned lower and bitcoin gave it all back, so the picture is little changed: still risk-off, still below $70,000. The US military has denied Iran's radar-strike claim, which takes some edge off the geopolitical worry. Zcash has held up better, back near $954. Next to watch: The US close at 21:00 UK and tonight's Friday ETF flow figures. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Bitcoin's PPI bounce fades as tech sell-off drags Wall Street

A softer-than-expected US producer price reading lifted bitcoin briefly above $70,000, but the gain vanished as Nvidia's leadership crisis pulled the Nasdaq lower and Treasury yields climbed.

Bitcoin rose to $70,190 on Kraken shortly after 13:30 UK on Friday, when the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that producer prices for final demand rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% economists had forecast. About $39 million of short positions were liquidated within an hour of the release, crypto.news reported, citing CoinGlass.

The relief was short-lived. US stocks opened higher at 14:30 UK and then turned lower, with the Nasdaq down about 1.6% and the S&P 500 down about 0.8% by late morning in New York, Yahoo Finance reported. Nvidia shares swung sharply after Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive, and the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.16%, its highest since October.

Bitcoin slid back to about $68,000 in the hour after the open and traded near $68,700 at 16:45 UK, according to Kraken data, down about 3.7% on the day.

The annual picture gave little comfort. Producer inflation reached 6.5% over 12 months, the largest annual increase since November 2022, and core prices rose 5.0%. Traders remain divided between a quarter-point and half-point Fed hike in December, crypto.news reported.

Selling from US spot bitcoin ETFs also continued. Thursday's final figures showed $284 million of net outflows, the sixth day in a row, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $204 million, according to SoSoValue data reported by PANews.

Friday's ETF flows and the US close at 21:00 UK are next. The Fed's December decision is due on 9 December.

A softer US PPI lifted bitcoin briefly above $70,000, but a Nvidia-led tech sell-off and 5.16% Treasury yields pushed it back to about $68,700. ETF outflows reached a sixth day, while the US denied Iran's radar-strike claim.

  1. 🔴 Developing Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin's jump above $70,000 on soft PPI fades after the US open (High confidence). Since this morning's $68,900, bitcoin rose to $70,190 on Kraken in the hour after the 13:30 UK PPI release, then fell to about $68,040 after the 14:30 US open and traded near $68,700 at 16:45 UK, down about 3.7% on the day. crypto.news, citing CoinGlass, said about $39 million of shorts were liquidated after the data and $1.42 billion of positions over 24 hours, 83% of them longs. Kraken (price data) crypto.news
  2. 🟠 New The Big Picture: US producer prices rise 0.3% in October, softer than forecast (High confidence). Final demand PPI rose 0.3% against 0.4% expected, with core also up 0.3%, in line. Over 12 months PPI rose 6.5% (forecast 6.6%), the biggest annual rise since November 2022, and core rose 5.0%. September was revised to 1.4%. It eases this week's inflation scare a little, after Tuesday's hot CPI. US Bureau of Labor Statistics StockTitan crypto.news
  3. 🟠 New Markets: Nasdaq falls about 1.6% as Nvidia turmoil and 5.16% yields weigh (Medium confidence). US stocks opened higher, then reversed: by late morning in New York the Nasdaq was down about 1.6%, the S&P 500 about 0.8% and the Dow 0.2%, Yahoo Finance reported. Nvidia fell as much as 14% at the open after Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The 10-year yield hit 5.16% and the VIX rose above 20. Bitcoin has tracked the Nasdaq lower. Yahoo Finance
  4. 🟠 Developing ETFs and Institutions: Thursday's ETF outflows finalised at $284 million, sixth day in a row (Medium confidence). This morning's early figure was $47.7 million with BlackRock and Fidelity still to report. SoSoValue data, reported by PANews, now puts Thursday's total net outflow at $284 million, with BlackRock's IBIT losing $204 million. Cointelegraph had already counted more than $2 billion leaving IBIT over the nine sessions to Wednesday, so Thursday extends that run to ten. KuCoin News (PANews, SoSoValue data) Cointelegraph
  5. 🟠 Outlook changed The Big Picture: US denies Iran's Bahrain radar-strike claim, says it downed two drones (High confidence). This morning the claim was unverified. The US military has since denied that any radar was hit, saying it shot down two one-way attack drones launched by the Revolutionary Guards towards Bahrain with no harm done, AP reported via Yahoo. Oil was little changed near $89 after Thursday's spike, per Yahoo Finance. The denial lowers the immediate escalation risk, though the Strait of Hormuz standoff continues. Yahoo News (AP) Al Jazeera
  6. 🟢 Developing Zcash Desk: Zcash recovers to about $954, outperforming bitcoin (High confidence). ZEC rose from about $938 this morning to a high of $992 on Kraken before settling near $954 at 16:45 UK, roughly flat on the day while bitcoin is down about 3.7%. No Zcash-specific news explained the move. Kraken (price data)
  7. 🟢 New Bitcoin Desk: Bitcoin treasury firm Nakamoto owes Kraken more than its market value (Medium confidence). Nakamoto owes Kraken 165 million USDT, backed by 3,030 pledged BTC worth about $208 million (roughly 126% of the debt) at $69,000, CoinDesk calculated. Its market value is about $104 million. A 12 November amendment pushed $60 million of repayments to December 2027. It shows how a falling bitcoin price squeezes leveraged treasury companies. CoinDesk
  8. 🟢 New Beyond the Watchlist: SpaceX–Tesla merger talks would combine about 30,220 bitcoin (Medium confidence). Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla are in merger talks, with an announcement possible as soon as December, CoinDesk said. Together they hold about 30,220 BTC (about $2.1 billion). A deal would combine existing holdings and needs no new buying. CoinDesk (citing Bloomberg)

Information only, not advice.

item.title: Fri 13 Nov 06:45 · risk-off · Bitcoin breaks below $70,000 as overnight liquidations top $1bn
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Bitcoin broke below $70,000 overnight and touched $67,500 on Kraken around 05:00 UK, its lowest since August, before steadying near $68,900.
  2. CoinDesk, citing CoinGlass, put 24-hour crypto liquidations above $1.2 billion, including about $677 million in bitcoin, as the fall through $70,000 forced out leveraged long positions.
  3. A stronger dollar, a 10-year Treasury yield above 5% and Iran's unverified claim of a strike on a US radar in Bahrain added pressure while the UK slept.

What changed: Last night bitcoin was holding near $71,500 and the question was whether it would bounce. It did not: it fell a further 3.5% or so in Asian hours, and the sell-off moved from a slow drift to a forced liquidation. Zcash dipped to $880 before recovering to about $938. Sentiment has hit 'extreme fear'. Next to watch: US producer prices (PPI) today at 13:30 UK, then Thursday's full ETF flow figures. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Bitcoin breaks below $70,000 as overnight liquidations top $1bn

Bitcoin fell through $70,000 during Asian trading on Friday and touched $67,500, its weakest level since August, as leveraged bets on higher prices were forced out.

Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 in the early hours of Friday, UK time, and reached $67,500 on Kraken shortly after 05:00. It was trading near $68,900 at 06:45, about 3.5% below its level at the close of US trading on Thursday evening.

More than $1.2 billion of crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including about $677 million in bitcoin, CoinDesk reported, citing CoinGlass. Nearly $500 million was forced out as the price fell through $70,000. Ether dropped below $2,000 for the first time since August.

CoinDesk linked the move to a stronger dollar, with the dollar index above 103, its highest since April 2025, and to rising bets on a December Fed rate hike after last week's hot consumer price data. Iran's Revolutionary Guards also claimed to have destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, a claim that could not be independently verified, investingLive reported.

The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 20, 'extreme fear', its lowest in more than four months, Cointelegraph reported. Preliminary Farside data showed further spot bitcoin ETF outflows on Thursday, with the largest funds still to report.

Zcash fell as low as $880 before recovering to about $938. US producer price figures are due at 13:30 UK.

CoinDesk Cointelegraph

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an air attack on a telecoms tower at Sirik on Iran's Hormuz coast, and warned firms working with the US over Hormuz oil shipments, investingLive reported. That would be a sixth straight day, after about $1.44 billion left in the previous five sessions and more than $2 billion left BlackRock's IBIT over nine sessions. Cointelegraph Cointelegraph (IBIT)

Bitcoin Magazine reported that Jane Street raised its Strategy stake by 54% to 4.1 million shares. Cointelegraph Bitcoin Magazine

ZEC slid from about $955 to $880 on Kraken between 03:00 and 05:00 UK as bitcoin broke down, then bounced to about $938 by 06:45. It is down about 2% since last night, a smaller fall than bitcoin's. No Zcash-specific news explained the move. Kraken (OHLC)

item.title: Thu 12 Nov 21:40 · risk-off · Stocks steady after Huang's exit but bitcoin stays near lows
item.description:
60-second briefing:

  1. Wall Street closed only about 0.4% lower and Nvidia cut its loss to 4.3%, after falling about 10% before the open on Jensen Huang's resignation.
  2. Bitcoin did not share the recovery: it ended the US session near $71,500, down about 3.3% on the day and close to Thursday's low of $71,133.
  3. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.10% and oil rose about 2.7% after President Trump said the US did not need a deal with Iran.

What changed: This afternoon the question was whether Huang's exit would spread through tech. It did not: the Nasdaq fell only 0.39% and Nvidia halved its loss. Bitcoin, though, stayed pinned near its low, so the gap between crypto and stocks widened. Higher yields and oil added to the rate pressure. Zcash was little changed at about $954. Next to watch: Thursday's US spot bitcoin ETF flows (due overnight), then US PPI on Friday 13 November at 13:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

Stocks steady after Huang's exit but bitcoin stays near lows

Wall Street closed only slightly lower on Thursday as Nvidia pared its losses, but bitcoin ended the US session near $71,500, close to its weakest level in about 12 weeks.

US shares closed modestly lower on Thursday after Nvidia's founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592, the Nasdaq Composite 0.39% and the Dow 0.36%, according to Yahoo Finance. Nvidia closed down 4.3% at $166.19, having traded about 10% lower before the open.

Bitcoin did not recover with stocks. It traded at about $71,500 on Kraken at 21:30 UK, down about 3.3% from the day's opening level and near Thursday's low of $71,133. The Block reported that more than $750 million of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, most of them bets on rising prices, citing CoinGlass.

Rates and energy added pressure. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.10%, up 0.10 percentage points, and US crude rose about 2.7% after President Trump said the US did not need a deal with Iran, Yahoo Finance reported.

In crypto company news, Binance said it had completed covering the $6.34 billion of assets stolen in its 29 October hack, using its own funds, Bitcoin Magazine reported. Rumble disclosed that it had sold about two-thirds of its bitcoin in the third quarter.

Zcash was about $954, little changed since the afternoon. Thursday's ETF flow figures are due overnight, and US producer prices follow on Friday at 13:30 UK.

Rumble's holdings fell from 293 BTC at the end of June to about 95 BTC on 30 September, according to its results, Bitcoin Magazine reported. It gave no reason. A small amount, but another company trimming bitcoin as cash shifts to AI businesses. Bitcoin Magazine
